title: Stability Echoes: SRE Weekly Ops Snapshot — 2027-05-11
body:
Purpose:
This is the SRE weekly ops snapshot covering the week of 2027-05-04 -> 2027-05-10. Focus areas: incidents and mitigations, SLO health and trends, on-call handoff notes, short experiments/ops work, and prioritized action items. This doc is intended to be concise for the weekly standup and as a handoff reference for next week’s responders.

Executive summary:
- Two customer-impacting incidents this week (INC-2027-045, INC-2027-046). Both related to tail-latency spikes on inference-gateway and eviction storms in kv-cache during scaledown windows.
- SLOs: inference-gateway p99 exceeded target twice (peak 560ms, target 300ms); request error rate marginally above SLO for a short window (0.95% vs 0.5% target) during the largest incident.
- Mitigations deployed: emergency autoscaler tuning (temporary raise in min replicas) + kv-cache eviction smoothing patch. Longer-term rollout planned next sprint.

Incident highlights:
1) INC-2027-045 — inference-gateway tail-latency spike (2027-05-06 10:12–11:04 UTC)
   - Scope: ~8% of requests to hosted/inference-gateway experienced >400ms extra tail latency; impact concentrated on customers with long-sequence workloads (seq > 2048).
   - Symptom: sudden increase in p99 and queuing across GPU-backed pools during normal traffic. No bulk errors, but timeouts increased for some downstream callers.
   - Immediate cause (hypothesis): autoscaler reacted to transient throughput drop and scaled down model-router pods leading to cold-KV-cache misses and 2x kernel re-warms on a subset of GPUs; combined with a batching timer edge-case producing larger-than-expected per-request serialization overhead.
   - Timeline (abridged):
     - 10:10 UTC — alert threshold crossed (p99 > 300ms).
     - 10:12 — oncall page; initial mitigation: raise min_replicas for pool-gpu-x to 4 (Jonah).
     - 10:22 — roll-forward of temporary autoscaler policy and increase in batching timeout (Maria).
     - 10:40 — p99 back to ~260ms; continued observation.
     - 11:04 — incident declared mitigated and monitoring tuned for recurrence.
   - Root-cause notes: interplay between scale-down thresholds and per-client cache lifetimes. When replicas dropped, worker-local KV caches were invalidated causing request-level recomputations and extra kernel startup cost.

2) INC-2027-046 — kv-cache eviction storm during regional maintenance (2027-05-09 03:30–04:05 UTC)
   - Scope: internal maintenance + scheduled node reboots triggered large-scale eviction events; increased backend load and transient error spikes for internal rerank pipelines.
   - Symptom: increased 5xxs for rerank & embed pipelines; autoscaler oscillation detected (scale down -> scale up cycles).
   - Mitigation: applied eviction-smoothing (limiting concurrent evictions per node) and staggered reboot plan. Reverted overly agressive rolling restart job.
   - Follow-up: persistence of some client state not ideal; need KV cache persistence design doc.

SLO health snapshot:
- inference-gateway latency SLOs: p50 35ms (ok), p95 120ms (ok), p99 340ms (breach window on 2027-05-06).
- error rate: 0.47% weekly avg; spike to 0.95% during incident 045. Target is <=0.5%.
- availability: Hosted API availability 99.96% for the week (within SLA but trending).
- Root cause trends: most tail-latency events correlate with two signals: (1) rapid scale-down events of GPU pools; (2) bursty long-sequence requests that force repeated KV-cache rebuilds.

Observability notes / investigation pointers:
- Dashboards: SLO-latency-trend, pool-autoscaler-actions, kv-cache-evictions (add filter by model family).
- Useful query: sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (pool, region) — look for spikes during scale events.
- Recording rule proposal (short): add an alert for concurrent_evictions_per_node > 5 sustained for 2m.

On-call handoff / next-week ops checklist:
- New oncall: Eleni Markou (primary) / Samuel Park (secondary) for 2027-05-10 -> 2027-05-17.
- Runbook check: confirm smoke tests complete for pool-gpu-x after any scale event (github PR linked below).
- Hot actions for oncall:
  1) If p99 > 400ms for >5m: raise min_replicas for affected GPU pool, inform platform (post in #sre-ops).
  2) If concurrent_evictions_per_node > 5: throttle node restarts, enable eviction-smoothing flag, open incident.
  3) During any maintenance window: ensure staggered reboots (stagger > 15m between same-pool nodes).
- Checklist: access to emergency-scaler-runbook, ticket templates for customer impact, contact list for infra team.

Short experiments / ops work in progress (WIP):
- Adaptive prefix-cache retention (Aisha + Jonah) — experiment to keep warm prefix caches for high-frequency customers for an extra 30s after scale-down. Canary on pool-gpu-y next week.
- Autoscaler hysteresis tuning (Maria) — reduce aggressive downscaling for pools with high KV churn. Testing different cooldown windows in staging this week.
- Batch timer heuristics (Samuel) — work to avoid large serialization windows for long-sequence requests; PR in review: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2145.

Action items (priority order):
- A1 (owner: Maria Gonzalez) — ship autoscaler cooling policy (#SRE-798) to prod, with rollback plan. Target: 2027-05-20.
- A2 (owner: Jonah Kim) — deploy prefix-cache retention canary to pool-gpu-y (small customer segment) and measure p99 improvement. Target: 2027-05-18.
- A3 (owner: Aisha Patel) — write short KB on scaledown impacts and hand it to Ops runbook. Target: 2027-05-14.
- A4 (owner: Samuel Park) — finalize batch-timer fix and merge after load test. Target: 2027-05-17.
- A5 (owner: Eleni Markou) — update oncall checklist and verify recovery playbook presence in Confluence. Target: 2027-05-13.

Customer communications:
- No broad customer email required. Outreach will be targeted to 3 customers who reported timeouts; CS lead to own communications (ticket INF-1123).

Notes / open questions:
- Should we persist a lightweight cache on a fast-networked NFS for quick rehydrate rather than per-pod ephemeral caches? Pros/cons engineering review needed.
- Are there billing-sensitive customers whose autoscaling behavior we need to treat differently (keep-min-replicas)? Product + SRE sync to map list.

Meeting cadence / next checkpoints:
- Quick follow-up sync (15m) Monday 2027-05-17 09:00 UTC to assess canary metrics. Invite: Aisha, Maria, Jonah, Samuel, Eleni.
- SRE weekly review (30m) Wednesday 2027-05-19 16:00 UTC for final decision on autoscaler policy changes.
